**Finding: Compliant** (preferred position met) — no redline proposed.

- **What I checked:** all "exclusive"/"sole"/"requirements" hits across the Agreement, Article II licence restrictions, the fee and volume provisions, the confidentiality/non-solicitation article, Article XXII (the defined "Right of First Refusal" flagged in the planner hints), and the General Provisions.
- **Result:** the licence is expressly *non-exclusive* (Preamble, Arts. II, IV, V), and nothing obliges us to source our Spot FX platform, liquidity or related services solely from SFG/E-Path FX, nor bars us from using competing platforms. The Article II covenants are scope-of-licence and IP-protection restrictions (no sublicensing, no third-party access, no reverse engineering), not restraints on our freedom to buy elsewhere, and there is no minimum-volume or all-requirements commitment in the fee schedule.
- **On the Right of First Refusal (Art. XXII):** it is a first-refusal right over a sale of our assets or a change of control, i.e. an exit/M&A restraint rather than a supply lock-in, so it does not engage this rule. It is worth reviewing under the change-of-control/assignment rule (together with Art. XX, which auto-terminates on a Change of Control absent Licensor consent), but I have not double-flagged it here.
